_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 15:04:02Z)**_

Yes — enable **On Show**, and leave On Hide and On Update off. Here's the reasoning:

## Which hooks

- **On Show — yes.** This is the canonical place (it's exactly what the example does in `Screen0_OnShow → APP_Screen_Initialize`). It fires inside `screenShow_Marvin()`, which runs *after* the widget tree is built but *before* the first `leUpdate()` renders into the canvases — so it's the right moment to bind canvases to hardware layers and show them. For marvin, `le_gen_init.c` calls `legato_showScreen(screenID_Marvin)` at boot, so this fires automatically on startup.
- **On Update — no.** It fires every Legato tick. We do *not* want per-tick canvas churn; the compositor acts on events (reveal, slide), not every frame. Hanging bind/show on OnUpdate would re-issue layer ops 55×/s for nothing.
- **On Hide — no (not yet).** marvin runs a single always-shown screen, so there's no teardown to react to. We'll revisit it only if we add a second screen or want to unbind/hide canvases on exit.

## What the screen file confirms

Your two layers, from `le_gen_screen_Marvin.c`:
- **`root0` → `leAddRootWidget(root0, 0)`** — full dashboard, `LE_DEFAULT_SCREEN_WIDTH × HEIGHT` (1280×800). → bind **canvas[0] → BASE (layer 0)**, show it.
- **`root1` → `leAddRootWidget(root1, 1)`** — `320×800`, holds `Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION`, which is created `setVisible(FALSE)/setEnabled(FALSE)` (the slide-out). → bind **canvas[1] → OVR1 (layer index 2, *not* HEO=1)**, positioned off-screen/hidden until the slide.

Note the `screenGetRoot_Marvin(lyrIdx)` mapping (0→root0, 1→root1) — with `baseCanvasID=0`, Legato layer *i* renders into `canvas[i]`, which is the natural fit.

## How we'll split the work

- **Buffer assignment** (our owned memory) → in a `Compositor_Initialize()` called from `APP_Initialize`, once: `gfxcSetPixelBuffer(0, 1280, 800, RGB565, &fb_base)` and `gfxcSetPixelBuffer(1, 320, 800, RGB565, &fb_nav)`, both static `.region_nocache`.
- **Bind + show** → in the On-Show hook: `gfxcSetLayer(0, 0)` + size/pos + `gfxcShowCanvas(0)` (dashboard up); `gfxcSetLayer(1, 2)` + position the nav layer hidden/off-screen.

**One caveat to verify on hardware:** `gfxcShowCanvas` no-ops until `GFX_CANVAS_Task` has flipped `gfxcState` to `RUNNING`. The canvas task and the Legato task are both priority 2, so on the very first boot show there's a small ordering race. If the dashboard comes up blank only on cold boot, the fix is to re-assert show (or gate on `gfxcGetStatus()`); the example gets away without it, so likely fine, but worth watching.

So: **enable On Show, regen.** Once you do, paste me the generated hook name (Composer emits something like `Marvin_OnShow()` for us to implement) and I'll write `ui/compositor.{h,c}` — buffer ownership + bind/show wired to that hook, nav layer staged for the slide. That's P1.

void APP_Initialize ( void )
{
    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;

    /* Logging shim: thin wrapper over libc printf with severity filter
     * and FreeRTOS-aware locking. Initialized first so subsequent code
     * (including video task startup) can use LOG_*. Default level is
     * INFO; flip to DEBUG via log_set_level() to enable verbose. */
    log_init(LOG_LEVEL_INFO);

    /* Spawn the video task. xTaskCreate is safe before vTaskStartScheduler;
     * the task runs once the scheduler picks it up. The video module owns
     * its capture-pipeline init (ISC, TC358743, backlight, HEO unbind),
     * the capture/display state machine, and the bridge-status polling. */
    Video_Initialize();

    /* Per-frame performance log: producer-side queues + drain task.
     * Init the queues here so any producer that posts before the
     * scheduler starts will not crash; the drain task is launched
     * separately by PerfLog_Start once the scheduler is up. */
    PerfLog_Initialize();

    /* App-side video layout: 720×480 video at (280, 76) on the 1280×800
     * panel — 1:1 with the bridge's typical 480p source, leaves a UI
     * strip below. Set before DisplayShow; the video module has no
     * default window of its own. */
    Video_SetWindow(280u, 76u, 720u, 480u);

    /* Default: arm the capture chain when source locks, and show video. */
    Video_CaptureEnable();
    Video_DisplayShow();

    /* Reference detector (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. M1 stub
     * publisher; real detection logic lands incrementally. Must follow
     * Video_Initialize since cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to the video frame
     * queue from inside its task. Detectors default disabled; explicitly
     * enable + select the active one for the timing pipeline. */
    Detector_Initialize();
    Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
    Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);

    /* M2 actuator path: fretboard_link owns the submit queue + FLEXCOM1
     * USART writer and the RX parse task. The FLEXCOM1 peripheral is brought
     * up by SYS_Initialize (FLEXCOM1_USART_Initialize), so this just arms the
     * ring-buffer RX notification and starts the link tasks. */
    FretboardLink_Initialize();

    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
     * FretboardLink_Send. */
    TimingPipeline_Initialize();

=== gfxcShowCanvas + gfxcSetPixelBuffer + gfxcSetLayer (apply path + state gating) ===
GFXC_RESULT gfxcSetPixelBuffer(unsigned int canvasID,
	const unsigned int width,
	const unsigned int height,
	const GFXC_COLOR_FORMAT format,
	void * buf)
{
	if (canvasID < CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ)
	{
		gfxPixelBufferCreate(width, height, format, (const void *)buf, &canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer);

		canvas[canvasID].layer.size.width = width;
		canvas[canvasID].layer.size.height = height;

		return GFX_SUCCESS;
	}

	return GFX_FAILURE;
}
---- show + setlayer ----
GFXC_RESULT gfxcShowCanvas(unsigned int canvasID)
{
	if (canvasID < CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ)
	{
		canvas[canvasID].active = GFX_TRUE;
		return GFX_SUCCESS;
	}

	return GFX_FAILURE;
}
GFXC_RESULT gfxcSetLayer(unsigned int canvasID, unsigned int layerID)
{
	if (canvasID < CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ &&
		canvas[canvasID].active == GFX_FALSE)
	{
		canvas[canvasID].layer.id = layerID;

		return GFX_SUCCESS;
	}

	return GFX_FAILURE;
}

=== GFX_CANVAS_Task body (RUNNING case) ===
void GFX_CANVAS_Task(void)
{
    switch(gfxcState)
    {
        case GFXC_INIT:
        {
#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_FX == true)
            effectsTimer = SYS_TIME_CallbackRegisterMS(effectsTimerCallback,
                           (uintptr_t) NULL,
                           effectsIntervalMS,
                           SYS_TIME_PERIODIC);
            SYS_TIME_TimerStop(effectsTimer);
#endif
            gfxcState = GFXC_RUNNING;
            break;
        }
        case GFXC_RUNNING:
        {
#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_FX == true)
            unsigned int i;

            //Process effects
            if (oldEffectsTick != effectsTick)
            {
                GFXC_RESULT gres = GFX_FAILURE;

                for (i = 0; i < CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ; i++)
                {
                    if (canvas[i].id != CANVAS_ID_INVALID)
                    {
                        GFXC_RESULT res = GFX_FAILURE;

#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_FADE_FX == true)
                        //Process alpha effects
                        switch(canvas[i].effects.fade.status)
                        {
                            case GFXC_FX_START:
                            {
                                canvas[i].effects.fade.status = GFXC_FX_RUN;

                                if(canvas[i].effects.cb != NULL)
                                    //call callback for status change START -> RUN
                                    canvas[i].effects.cb(canvas[i].id,
                                        GFXC_FX_FADE,
                                        GFXC_FX_RUN,
                                        canvas[i].effects.parm);
                                        //no break, start running effect;
                            }
                            case GFXC_FX_RUN:
                            {
                                res = gfxcProcessFadeEffect(&canvas[i]);
                                if (gres == GFX_FAILURE)
                                    gres = res;
                                break;
                            }
                            default:
                                break;
                        }
#endif
#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_MOVE_FX == true)
                        //Process move effects
                        switch(canvas[i].effects.move.status)
                        {
                            case GFXC_FX_START:
                            {
                                canvas[i].effects.move.status = GFXC_FX_RUN;

                                if (canvas[i].effects.cb != NULL)
                                    //call callback for status change START -> RUN
                                    canvas[i].effects.cb(canvas[i].id,
                                        GFXC_FX_MOVE,
                                        GFXC_FX_RUN,
                                        canvas[i].effects.parm);
                                    //no break, start running effect;
                            }
                            case GFXC_FX_RUN:
                            {
                                res = gfxcProcessMoveEffect(&canvas[i]);
                                if (gres == GFX_FAILURE)
                                    gres = res;
                                break;
                            }
                            default:
                                break;
                        }
#endif
                    }
                }

                if (gres == GFX_FAILURE)
                    SYS_TIME_TimerStop(effectsTimer);

                oldEffectsTick = effectsTick;
            }
#endif
            break;
        }
        default:
            break;
    }
}

=== _gfxcCanvasUpdate (how an active canvas programs its layer) ===
GFXC_RESULT _gfxcCanvasUpdate(unsigned int canvasID)
{
    gfxIOCTLArg_Value argValue;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setBaseAddressParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setLayerEnabledParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setColorModeParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerSize setResParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerPosition setPositionParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerSize setSizeParm;
    gfxIOCTLArg_LayerValue setAlphaParm;

    if (canvasID < CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ &&
        canvas[canvasID].layer.id != LAYER_ID_INVALID &&
        gfxDispCtrlr != NULL &&
        gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl != NULL)
    {
        setBaseAddressParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        if (canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.pixels != NULL)
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer = canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.pixels;
        else
        {
            argValue.value.v_int = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
            gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_SET_ACTIVE_LAYER, (gfxIOCTLArg_Value*) &argValue);

            gfxDispCtrlr->ioctl(GFX_IOCTL_GET_FRAMEBUFFER, (gfxIOCTLArg_Value*) &argValue);
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer = argValue.value.v_pbuffer->pixels;
        }

        setColorModeParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setColorModeParm.value.v_uint = (unsigned int) canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode;

		//This is the physical resolution of the layer pixel buffer
        setResParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setResParm.width = canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.size.width;
        setResParm.height = canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.size.height;

        setSizeParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setSizeParm.width = canvas[canvasID].layer.size.width;
        setSizeParm.height = canvas[canvasID].layer.size.height;

        setPositionParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setPositionParm.x = canvas[canvasID].layer.pos.xpos;
        setPositionParm.y = canvas[canvasID].layer.pos.ypos;

        setAlphaParm.layer.id = canvas[canvasID].layer.id;
        setAlphaParm.value.v_uint = canvas[canvasID].layer.alpha;

#if (CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_WINDOW_CLIPPING == true)
		//align offsets for non-32bpp frames
        if (gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode].size != 4)
            setPositionParm.x &= ~0x3;

        if (setPositionParm.x < 0)
        {
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer += abs(setPositionParm.x) *
                    gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode].size;

            setSizeParm.width += setPositionParm.x;
            setPositionParm.x = 0;
        }

        if (setPositionParm.y < 0)
        {
            setBaseAddressParm.value.v_pointer += abs(setPositionParm.y) *
                    setResParm.width *
                    gfxColorInfoTable[canvas[canvasID].pixelBuffer.mode].size;

            setSizeParm.height += setPositionParm.y;
            setPositionParm.y = 0;
        }

```c
#include "ui/compositor.h"

#include <stdint.h>

#include "gfx/canvas/gfx_canvas_api.h"
#include "gfx/legato/generated/screen/le_gen_screen_Marvin.h"

/* Two layers on the Marvin screen (le_gen_screen_Marvin.c):
 *   layer 0 (root0) — full-screen dashboard
 *   layer 1 (root1) — 320x800 navigation panel (slide-out)
 * Canvas id == Legato layer index (baseCanvasID is 0). */
#define CANVAS_BASE   0u
#define CANVAS_NAV    1u

#define BASE_W   1280u
#define BASE_H   800u
#define NAV_W    320u
#define NAV_H    800u

/* XLCDC layer indices in drvLayer/layerOrder order: BASE, HEO, OVR1, OVR2.
 * HEO (1) is the live camera and is off-limits to the compositor. */
#define HW_BASE   0u
#define HW_OVR1   2u

#define FB_NOCACHE   __attribute__((section(".region_nocache"), aligned (32)))

static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_base[BASE_W * BASE_H];
static uint16_t FB_NOCACHE s_fb_nav[NAV_W * NAV_H];

void Compositor_Initialize(void)
{
    /* Own the canvas surface memory: RGB565 to match the panel, non-cached so
     * the 2D engine and LCDC DMA read CPU-rendered pixels coherently. Replaces
     * the generated NULL-buffer template in gfx_canvas_config.c. */
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_BASE, BASE_W, BASE_H, GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_base);
    gfxcSetPixelBuffer(CANVAS_NAV,  NAV_W,  NAV_H,  GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565, s_fb_nav);

    /* Drive the canvas state machine to RUNNING now, before the scheduler, so
     * Legato's first blit into a canvas is not dropped by the RUNNING gate in
     * GFXC_BlitBuffer. With effects disabled the canvas task otherwise flips
     * this only on its first tick, which races Legato's first render. */
    GFX_CANVAS_Task();
}

void Marvin_OnShow(void)
{
    /* Dashboard: full-screen BASE layer, shown. */
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_BASE, 0, 0);
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_BASE, BASE_W, BASE_H);
    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_BASE, HW_BASE);
    gfxcShowCanvas(CANVAS_BASE);
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_BASE);

    /* Navigation: bound to OVR1, sized, but left hidden (canvas stays inactive
     * so OVR1 is programmed disabled). The slide-out reveal is wired later. */
    gfxcSetWindowPosition(CANVAS_NAV, 0, 0);
    gfxcSetWindowSize(CANVAS_NAV, NAV_W, NAV_H);
    gfxcSetLayer(CANVAS_NAV, HW_OVR1);
    gfxcCanvasUpdate(CANVAS_NAV);
}

P1 compositor is written and wired. Here's what landed:

**New `ui/compositor.{h,c}`** — owns the canvas surface memory and presents the dashboard:
- Two static `.region_nocache` RGB565 buffers: `s_fb_base` (1280×800, ~2.0 MB) and `s_fb_nav` (320×800, ~0.5 MB).
- `Compositor_Initialize()` — assigns those buffers to canvas 0/1 via `gfxcSetPixelBuffer` (replacing the NULL template), then calls `GFX_CANVAS_Task()` once to flip the canvas state machine to `RUNNING` **before the scheduler** — this defuses the cold-boot race (Legato's `GFXC_BlitBuffer` is `RUNNING`-gated, so a first render before the canvas task ticked would otherwise be dropped → blank).
- `Marvin_OnShow()` (the hook you enabled) — binds canvas 0 → **BASE (layer 0)**, shows it (dashboard up); binds canvas 1 → **OVR1 (layer 2, not HEO)**, sized but left hidden (canvas inactive → OVR1 programmed disabled), staged for the slide-out.

**Wired in:** `Compositor_Initialize()` called from `APP_Initialize` (after `log_init`, pre-scheduler); `ui/compositor.c` added to `user.cmake`; include added to `app.c`.

Why this works, confirmed against the generated canvas code:
- `_gfxcCanvasUpdate` is synchronous and ungated, and sets `enable = canvas.active` — so BASE (shown) enables, NAV (not shown) stays disabled.
- Buffers are assigned pre-scheduler, so Legato never renders into a NULL canvas (which would crash — note canvas 1 *must* have a buffer because Legato renders root1 into it every frame regardless of display state).

3. **`song_list_demo`** attaches to `root0` (BASE) — it'll render on the dashboard layer as before.

No conflicts — the only other references are the generated callback registrations (`setPressedEventCallback`/`setReleasedEventCallback`), which is exactly how our definitions get wired in. The GUITAR_STRUM handlers live in `manual_input.c`, confirming the "ui shim defines Marvin button events" idiom (ours live in `compositor.c`, next to `Marvin_OnShow`).

## What's wired

- **`Compositor_NavOpen()`** — makes `Marvin_PANEL_NAVIGATION` visible+enabled (so Legato repaints it into canvas 1 and routes touch to it), positions canvas 1 at (0,0), shows it, updates → **OVR1 enabled, nav menu appears**.
- **`Compositor_NavClose()`** — hides canvas 1 + updates → OVR1 disabled, then makes the panel invisible/disabled.
- **`event_Marvin_BUTTON_SYSYEM_NAVIGATION_OnPressed`** → `NavOpen()` (button is on the dashboard/BASE).
- **`event_Marvin_BUTTON_NAV_DASHBOARD_OnReleased`** → `NavClose()` (button is inside the nav menu/OVR1).

Build & test — expected: tap the nav button → menu appears over the dashboard on OVR1; tap Dashboard inside it → menu disappears. Touch on the in-menu button should route because the nav panel is a real Legato widget on layer 1, and OVR1 sits at (0,0) so `LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE` syncs Legato's pick rect to match.

## Honest caveat: this is an instant show/hide, **not** a slide (yet)

Canvas effects are **off** (`CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_FX false`), so `gfxcStartEffectMove` can't drive an animation — its stepper is compiled out. I deliberately did **not** pre-wire `gfxcStartEffectMove`, because with FX off it would set the move state and never step it → the menu would get stuck off-screen and never appear. So a snap is the correct functional first cut. Two ways to make it actually slide:

- **A — re-enable canvas Move FX** (MCC: Effects Settings + Move on, regen). Then `NavOpen/Close` call `gfxcStartEffectMove(CANVAS_NAV, …, -320→0 …)` and the canvas task animates it, hardware-paced. Least code, purpose-built. *Reverses our earlier "FX off" decision* — but a slide is exactly the case the doc said canvas FX earns its weight, so it's defensible (I'd update the journal).
- **B — keep FX off, self-driven stepper.** Enable the Marvin screen's **On Update** hook; I write a small stepper in `Marvin_OnUpdate()` that advances the nav window X toward a target each `leUpdate` (~55 Hz) via `gfxcSetWindowPosition` + `gfxcCanvasUpdate`. Stays consistent with "do our own," no FX task.

Not committed — please build/test the snap first. If it opens/closes cleanly, tell me which slide path (A or B) you want and I'll wire it. My lean: **A** if you want it smooth with minimal code; **B** if you'd rather keep the FX engine off.

Here's where the diagnosis stands. I've **ruled out** the usual regen suspects by inspecting the committed/staged tree:

- **`LE_NO_CACHE_ATTR` `-D` intact** in `user.cmake`.
- **Not the compositor ordering** — `legato_showScreen` only sets `changingToScreen`; the real show (and `Marvin_OnShow`) happens post-scheduler from the LEGATO task, *after* `Compositor_Initialize` has assigned buffers. So the compositor isn't the early-boot suspect.

Zero marvin DBGU output means it's hanging in `SYS_Initialize`, **before** `log_init`. I can't pinpoint that by static analysis — I need one fact from the hardware.

## Fastest definitive step: halt over JTAG and read the PC

The board is JTAG-debuggable (your `sam9x75-chybrid.cfg`). With the board hung, attach and halt:

```
arm-none-eabi-gdb
(gdb) target remote :3333
(gdb) monitor halt
(gdb) bt
(gdb) info registers pc
```

The backtrace tells us exactly which init is spinning (or which fault handler it's stuck in) in one shot — guessing further is wasteful when the answer is right there.

## Parallel bisect: regen vs. our code

To localize without JTAG, neutralize the compositor and rebuild:
- Comment out `Compositor_Initialize();` in `app.c`, and stub `Marvin_OnShow`/the two event handlers to empty bodies.
- **Boots + logs (blank screen)** → the fault is in our compositor/canvas-present path.
- **Still hangs, no log** → the fault is the MCC canvas/XLCDC/Legato regen itself, independent of our code (more likely, given it rearchitected the display driver).

## Two things to confirm first (cheap)

1. **Did marvin actually get loaded+jumped via JTAG?** That bootstrap banner ("Can load application via JTAG and jump") is the INIT_AND_STOP variant — on a bare power-cycle it stops there and marvin never runs. If you only power-cycled and didn't run your `load-ram` step, "no marvin output" is expected and there's no bug. 
2. **Did the build link cleanly** (compositor.c compiled, no undefined `Marvin_OnShow`)? If the link failed and you flashed/ran a stale image, that changes everything.

Run the JTAG halt (or tell me the answers to #1/#2) and I'll take it from there. My working hypothesis: a *different* re-apply patch got clobbered by the full regen (the journal lists ~10) — but the PC at hang will confirm or kill that immediately.

There it is — busy-wait loops on LCD status, including `while(XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_ATTRE);` (line 983) which waits for the LCDC to latch an attribute update (needs vsync). `XLCDC_Initialize` now calls `XLCDC_SetupOVR1Layer()`/`XLCDC_SetupOVR2Layer()` **before** `XLCDC_Start()`. If the OVR setup commits attributes and spins on `ATTRE` before the display is scanning, it hangs forever — early in `SYS_Initialize`, before any output. Let me look at those functions vs. the base/HEO setup that works.

That's the root cause — nice call. Heap exhaustion, not the XLCDC path (my OVR theory was wrong; BASE/HEO use the same `ATTRE`/`SIP` wait pre-Start, so OVR was symmetric). _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 15:44:32Z)**_

Now the full mechanism is clear — and there's an important durable fix hiding here. `configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK = 1`, and `vApplicationMallocFailedHook()` is the MCC default:

```c
taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS();
for( ;; ) { /* Do Nothing */ }
```

So when the canvas regen pushed a `pvPortMalloc` past the 40 KB heap **during `SYS_Initialize`** (before `APP_Initialize`/`log_init` at initialization.c:499), this hook fired and spun with interrupts off → dead, **zero output**. That's exactly the silent presentation — same footgun class as the `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` already flagged in the journal. Let me confirm whether the heap size is regen-safe.

Documented. Summary of where this landed and the durable follow-ups:

## Root cause (confirmed)
The canvas regen's added dynamic demand (the `GFX_CANVAS_Task` + OSAL/driver allocations on the 4-layer/canvas display path) pushed `pvPortMalloc` past the 40 KB `heap_1` **during `SYS_Initialize`**. The MCC-default `vApplicationMallocFailedHook` (`taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS(); for(;;){}`) then spun with interrupts off, *before* `log_init` — so it looked like a dead board. `40960 → 100000` gives the headroom. Your heap hypothesis was right; my XLCDC theory was wrong (BASE/HEO use the same pre-`Start` `ATTRE`/`SIP` wait, so OVR was symmetric).

## Two things worth fixing now (both recorded in the journal)

1. **Make the heap bump regen-safe — important.** `configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE` is **not** in `FreeRTOS.yml`; it's a raw literal in the generated `FreeRTOSConfig.h`. So your edit is an MCC re-apply patch (joins patch #8) and the **next regen will silently revert it → the hang comes back**. Check the FreeRTOS component in MCC for a "Total Heap Size" field — if it's there, set 100000 there so it survives regen; if not, it goes on the re-apply list.

2. **Kill the silent-failure footgun.** Both `vApplicationMallocFailedHook` and `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` are silent IRQ-off spins. A one-line DBGU marker before the spin would have turned this whole bisect into an instant "MALLOC FAILED" read. This was already flagged for the stack hook; the malloc hook just proved it bites.

Optional: log `xPortGetFreeHeapSize()` once at boot so the next heap wall is visible instead of silent — 100000 is +60 KB, generous, but you're now flying without a gauge.

Want me to:
- patch `freertos_hooks.c` (both hooks → DBGU marker + LOG_ERR), and
- add an `xPortGetFreeHeapSize()` line to the boot log?

Both are quick. Then you can pop the compositor stash and get back to the nav-menu spin. (Nothing committed — you're mid-work with the stash pending.)

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 16:09:03Z)**_

Both answered, with evidence.

## Q1 — the flash is **ours**, not MGS

Confirmed from `Compositor_NavOpen`'s ordering:

```c
setVisible(TRUE);        // invalidates the panel — but Legato repaints it into
                         // canvas 1 only on the NEXT leUpdate (LEGATO task)
gfxcShowCanvas + Update; // enables OVR1 NOW, pointing at s_fb_nav
```

So OVR1 turns on **before** Legato has repainted the freshly-made-visible panel into `s_fb_nav`. For ~1 frame the overlay shows the *stale* buffer (on first open: the root1 background with the menu still hidden; on later opens: the previous contents), then Legato paints the real menu. Classic "enable the layer before its buffer is rendered" race. No MGS widget is misbehaving.

**Fix (design-aligned): pre-render and park.** Keep the nav content rendered into `s_fb_nav` continuously (panel stays visible in Legato), and reveal purely via the canvas layer. Then "open" shows an already-correct buffer — zero flash, and it's exactly the "pre-render in RAM, point a layer at it" model from the doc. The wrinkle: a permanently-visible+enabled panel would let Legato route touches to it even when closed (stealing taps from the dashboard's left column). Clean gate: drive **touch and visibility off the canvas window position** — closed = position the nav canvas off-screen (Legato's layer-1 pick rect follows it via `LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE`, so taps fall through to BASE), open = position at (0,0). That also *is* your slide. Quick alternative if you want minimal change now: defer the `gfxcShowCanvas` by one frame (do it from `Marvin_OnUpdate` the tick after `setVisible`), so the paint lands first.

## Q2 — drop the toggle buttons; the state shouldn't live in the widget

What's happening: a Legato button's `toggleable` mode ties Pressed/Released to toggle-state transitions, which is why "released only fires when it goes false." Toggle buttons are an on/off control, not a radio selector, and Legato buttons have **no** built-in grouping — so you're left hand-rolling the interlock against confusing edge events. Wrong tool.

Three options, ranked for your case (a short, static set of screens):

1. **Momentary buttons + app-owned active state (my recommendation).** Turn `toggleable` *off*. Each button's `OnReleased` fires cleanly on tap-up = "select screen N". Hold the active screen in compositor/app state (`s_active_screen`), and reflect it by highlighting the active button (scheme or `setPressed`). Interlock is one variable. You keep the buttons you already laid out; no new widget, no regen beyond un-toggling. The key idea: **the widget is a momentary trigger; the *app* owns "which screen is active."**

2. **`leRadioButtonWidget` + `leRadioButtonGroup` (Legato-native).** The radio-button widget *is* in-tree (`widget/radiobutton/`, with a `radiobutton_group`) — purpose-built single-active interlock and selection tracking, so Legato owns the state for you. Cost: it's disabled (`LE_RADIOBUTTON_WIDGET_ENABLED 0`) — enable it in MGS and restyle the nav entries as radio buttons (regen). Best if you'd rather not manage active-state yourself.

3. **Custom list widget (song_list-style) — not recommended here.** A virtualized list earns its keep for the *scrollable, data-driven* 64-song catalog. The nav menu is a short, fixed, hand-placed set — a custom list would be over-engineering. Reserve that pattern for scrollable data.

My call: **option 1.** It's the least friction (you already have the buttons), gives clean per-tap events, and putting "active screen" in app state rather than widget toggle-state is the correct separation — it also makes the highlight and the eventual screen-switching logic straightforward.

Want me to implement: (a) the parked-render flash fix in the compositor (closed = off-screen position, which also seeds the slide), and (b) convert the nav buttons to momentary + a small `compositor`-owned active-screen interlock with highlight? I can do both; tell me if you'd prefer radio buttons for (b) instead.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 16:18:53Z)**_

Fixed. The change: **stop toggling `setVisible`/`setEnabled` around the show** — that toggle was the flash. Now the nav panel stays visible+enabled permanently, so Legato renders it into `s_fb_nav` continuously and the buffer is always current. Open/close just move and enable/disable the OVR1 layer:

- **`Marvin_OnShow`** — nav panel made visible+enabled once; canvas bound to OVR1, parked **off-screen left** (`x = -320`) and hidden.
- **`Compositor_NavOpen`** — slot layer to `(0,0)` + show. Buffer already painted → no flash.
- **`Compositor_NavClose`** — hide + park off-screen.

Parking off-screen (rather than toggling `enabled`) also handles touch: Legato's layer-1 pick rect follows the layer position via `LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE`, so the closed nav sits off-screen and can't intercept dashboard taps — *and* it seeds the eventual slide-in (animate `x` from −320 → 0).

**One thing to watch on hardware:** this assumes Legato offsets touch picking by the layer's `driverPosition` (standard multi-layer behavior). If a *closed* nav still eats taps in the left strip, that assumption is off and we'll gate touch differently — but that falls into the nav-button rework you're deferring anyway.

Build/test: hamburger should open the nav cleanly (no flash), Dashboard button closes it. Once you confirm, we commit as the working canvas example — want me to stage + commit (compositor + the heap/hooks changes) at that point, or will you?

## On the bigger architecture question (deferred, per your ask)

Quick lean to chew on later: **yes** — develop each full-screen view (dashboard, song/mode dialog) as its own MGS Screen so MGS generates all the widget bring-up; that's exactly what MGS is good at. The nav panel being *cross-screen* is the one piece that doesn't fit the one-Screen-at-a-time model — options are (a) a dedicated MGS Screen rendered onto its own canvas/OVR layer and composited over whichever base Screen is active (the compositor's whole reason for being), or (b) a shared widget instantiated into each Screen. (a) fits what we've built. I'll think it through properly when we come back — it deserves a journal entry and probably shapes how `screenShow_*`/canvas mapping works per Screen. For now, flash is fixed and we're clear to commit.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 17:14:40Z)**_

Wired. Your approach is exactly right — and Legato's radio group makes it clean. What I added in `compositor.c`:

- **`nav_radio_selected` / `nav_radio_deselected`** — one shared callback pair that swaps the button's scheme to `SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_SELECTED` / `_UNSELECTED`. Because the group fires *Deselected* on the outgoing button and *Selected* on the incoming one, the highlight stays correct with no need to track the previous selection.
- **`nav_buttons_init()`** (called from `Marvin_OnShow`) — registers those callbacks on all six nav buttons, and syncs the initial scheme to the group's current selection (Dashboard is `setSelected` at init, *before* our callbacks exist, so we set its SELECTED scheme explicitly).

No MGS regen needed — registering the callbacks in code is lighter than enabling Selected/Deselected events on six buttons (which would generate 12 stub decls). The division of labor: **I own the swap logic; you own the colors** in the two schemes via MGS.

Build/test: tapping a nav entry should highlight it (SELECTED scheme) and un-highlight the previous one; Dashboard starts highlighted.

Note for later — `nav_radio_selected` is exactly the seam where **screen-switching** will hook: the same callback can dispatch on which button fired (`btn == Marvin_BUTTON_NAV_LOGS` …) to swap the active base-screen/canvas. That ties into the deferred "panels as separate MGS Screens" architecture, so I'd leave the navigation action out until we settle that.

Not committed — test first. Want me to fold this into a commit once you've confirmed the highlight works, or keep going?

    leResult res;
    
    LE_ASSERT_THIS();
    
    if(_this->selected == LE_TRUE)
        return LE_FAILURE;

    if(_this->group == NULL)
        return LE_SUCCESS;
   
    _invalidateContents(_this);
    
    res = leRadioButtonGroup_SelectButton(_this->group, _this);
    
    if(res == LE_SUCCESS)
    {
        _invalidateContents(_this);
    }

#if LE_DEBUG == 1
    _leDebugNotify_WidgetPropertyChanged((leWidget*)_this);
#endif

    return res;
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 17:30:40Z)**_

Found it — and you're right to question the radio path. The selection mechanic **is** built in (no events needed): `handleTouchUpEvent` calls `leRadioButtonGroup_SelectButton` directly. But look at the gate:

```c
// handleTouchUpEvent (legato_widget_radiobutton.c:526)
_leRadioButtonWidget_GetImageRect(_this, &imgRect, &imgSrcRect);
leRectClip(&imgRect, &widgetRect, &clipRect);     // clipRect = the INDICATOR IMAGE area
...
if(leRectContainsPoint(&clipRect, &pt) == LE_TRUE)
    leRadioButtonGroup_SelectButton(_this->group, _this);   // only selects if tap is on the image
```

**A Legato radio button only registers a tap on its indicator-image rect — not the whole row.** Your nav entries are 287×56 with a small left icon, so taps on the text/body do nothing. Regular buttons accept a tap anywhere on the widget (that's why those worked). This is a widget-behavior mismatch, not a missing hook — and to answer directly: **no, you don't need to enable events, and the scheme callback isn't the problem** (the group fires `select`/`deselect` → our callbacks, but only *after* `SelectButton` runs, which the image-rect gate is blocking).

So `leRadioButtonGroup` ends up being a poor fit for full-row nav entries. Two ways forward:

**Option A — go back to regular `leButton` + a tiny app interlock (my recommendation).** Whole-row touch works (proven). Keep the single-active behavior in app code: each button's `OnReleased` → mark it active, set its scheme `SELECTED` and the others `UNSELECTED`. That's ~10 lines in the compositor, and I already have the scheme-swap helper — it just gets called from the button handlers instead of radio events. This is exactly the "widget is a momentary trigger, app owns the active state" path from before; the radio detour confirmed why it's the better fit here.

**Option B — keep radio buttons, make the whole row clickable.** Either (i) enlarge/position the radio image to fill the 287×56 cell in MGS (clickable area = image rect, so a full-cell image = full-row tap), or (ii) subclass the radio widget and override `handleTouchUpEvent` to use the widget rect instead of the image rect (like `song_list` overrides its vtable). (ii) is real code and loses the "native" simplicity.

My call is **A** — least code, reliable whole-row taps, and you keep the schemes/strings/icons you already authored (just switch the widget type back). Want me to wire option A (convert the handlers + a 6-entry active-state interlock with the scheme swap)? If you'd rather not touch MGS again and prefer keeping radio buttons, I'll do B(i) guidance or B(ii) the subclass.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 19:33:06Z)**_

Definitive answer from the code: **no — a non-toggleable button can't be held pressed programmatically.** Look at `setPressed`:

```c
if(pressed == LE_TRUE) {
    if(pressedEvent) pressedEvent(_this);
    if(_this->toggleable == LE_TRUE)
        _this->state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED;   // only toggleable "sticks"
    else
        if(_this->releasedEvent) releasedEvent(_this);  // momentary: fires released immediately
}
```

On a momentary button, `setPressed(true)` just synthesizes a click (fires pressed → immediately released) and leaves `state = LE_BUTTON_STATE_UP`. Only a **toggleable** button enters the sticky `LE_BUTTON_STATE_TOGGLED`. So a momentary button's pressed visual is purely transient touch feedback — it never persists to show "this is the selected screen."

So **yes, keep the two schemes** — that's the right call, and it's already what's in the code. The split:
- **Transient**: the button's own pressed image/offset gives the brief tap feedback (automatic, no scheme needed).
- **Persistent**: `nav_on_release` swaps `SCHEME_NAV_BUTTON_SELECTED` / `UNSELECTED` to show which entry is active.

You'd only get "pressed = selected" for free if you went back to **toggleable** buttons (which stick via `TOGGLED`) — but that's the path with the awkward released-only-on-untoggle events and no group interlock, which you already rejected. Momentary + two schemes is the clean combo.

Net: **no change needed** — what we just wired is correct. Don't remove the schemes. Build/test the current version (hamburger toggles, tap any entry to switch the highlight); once it looks right, we commit.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 19:45:33Z)**_

Confirmed enough to answer — and the key point: **your behavior is already right; this is a color-mapping issue, not a logic one.**

## Press vs release — commit on release is standard for *both* touch and mouse

This isn't a mouse-only convention. iOS, Android/Material, and desktop all **commit the action on release (touch-up over the element)**, with the press only showing transient feedback. The reason is *cancel-by-slide-off*: you can press, change your mind, slide your finger off, and lift — and nothing fires. Press-to-commit throws that away. Press-to-act is reserved for cases where the press *is* the action (keyboards, your STRUM buttons — momentary actuation). Navigation/selection → commit on release. So `nav_on_release` is correct; keep it.

## Why it looks off right now

You've mapped the **selected color (blue) onto the unselected-pressed state**, so:
- Press an unselected item → it turns blue → *looks selected* immediately.
- The actually-selected item stays blue until you release.
- → two blue items during the press.

The timing is correct (selection moves on release); the colors just conflate "I'm pressing this" with "this is selected." There are really **three** states to express, and you've only got two colors doing the work of three.

## Recommended scheme mapping

| State | Color |
|---|---|
| Unselected, idle | black |
| Unselected, **pressed** (transient "will select on release") | a **neutral feedback shade** — dark gray, *not* blue |
| Selected (pressed *and* released) | blue |

Now: press a candidate → it shows gray, the old selection stays blue; release → candidate goes blue, old goes black. **Blue only ever marks the committed selection**, and it appears to "move" on release — exactly the mental model you described. Selected staying blue for both states is right (re-tapping the active item shouldn't flicker).

Your "make unselected black when pressed too" is the **simpler alternative**: no press feedback at all, highlight swaps atomically on release. Clean and unambiguous, but you lose the touch acknowledgment that the tap registered. For a nav drawer that's acceptable — but most polished touch UIs keep *some* press feedback, so I'd lean toward the distinct-gray version over killing it.

Either way, no code change — it's all in the two schemes you own in MGS. And worth a quick test of the payoff: **press an entry, slide off, release → should select nothing and revert the press highlight** (Legato fires `released` only when you lift over the widget). That slide-off cancel is the whole reason release-commit wins for touch.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-25 19:57:35Z)**_

Confirmed — and it splits cleanly into two tiers:

## Widget events → yes, runtime-registerable (your DI instinct is right)
Button pressed/released, radio selected/deselected, slider value-changed, list selection, raw touch — all stored as function pointers in the widget with `setXxxEventCallback()` vtable setters:
```c
(*setReleasedEventCallback)(THIS_TYPE*, leButtonWidget_ReleasedEvent cb);
```
MGS "events" are just **sugar**: the generated screen init calls `setReleasedEventCallback(widget, event_Screen_Widget_OnReleased)` and emits the extern. You can make that exact setter call yourself anytime after the widget exists — which is what we did for the six nav buttons. So DI-in-code is fully equivalent and often cleaner.

## Screen lifecycle events (On Show / Hide / Update) → no, *not* runtime-registerable
These are emitted as a **direct hardcoded call** to a symbol you define:
```c
Marvin_OnShow(); // raise event
```
There's no `setScreenShowCallback`. Enabling the event in MGS just adds/removes that direct call; you can't swap it at runtime. (The only "set...Show" in the tree is an unrelated listwheel property.)

## So the clean pattern is a hybrid
You can't avoid the one screen hook — but that's actually a feature: **`Marvin_OnShow` is your composition root.** It's the single fixed seam MGS gives you, and from inside it you runtime-register everything else in code. That's exactly the structure we have: one MGS screen hook → `compositor.c` → registers the nav button sinks. Logic stays in your module either way; DI just moves the *binding* there too.

## Trade-offs, since you're thinking architecturally
**Runtime/DI registration** wins when:
- one handler serves many widgets (6 nav buttons → one `nav_on_release`),
- you want all UI wiring in one greppable module, not scattered MGS stubs,
- you want it to survive regen without re-applying (the binding lives in your code, not the regenerated screen init).

**MGS events** win when a designer should *see/manage* the wiring in the tool, or for genuinely one-off handlers.

Two caveats for the runtime approach:
1. **Timing** — register only after the widgets exist. The screen On-Show hook is the natural place (widgets are built by then). Don't try it in `APP_Initialize`.
2. **Teardown** — `screenHide_*` destroys the widget tree, so widget pointers/registrations die with it. If you register in On-Show, that's self-healing (re-runs each show). This is the same gotcha already flagged in the journal for `manual_input`'s single-screen assumption — and it'll matter directly when we move to per-screen canvases, since each screen's On-Show becomes its own composition root.

Net: lean on runtime widget-event registration as your default (it's the cleaner DI), and treat each screen's On-Show as the one MGS-given entry point you wire from.

Strong instinct — and you're right that one generic compositor will muddle as views multiply. But before settling module boundaries, there are **two hard constraints** that should drive the design, plus one insight that makes them work *for* you:

## The constraints
1. **Legato renders only the *one active screen* per frame.** `legato_showScreen` tears down the current screen's widget tree and builds the next. So two Legato Screens can't both be live simultaneously — switching to one freezes/destroys the other.
2. **4 LCDC layers total** (BASE, HEO=camera, OVR1, OVR2). Camera owns HEO. So at most ~3 UI surfaces composited at once.

## The insight that resolves them
Decouple **"what has touch focus"** from **"what's visible"**:
- **Active Legato screen = the focus** (the thing being interacted with + live-rendering).
- **Everything else visible = parked canvases** the LCDC composites in hardware (the camera already works this way; a backgrounded view's canvas keeps its last-rendered pixels).

Legato's one-screen limit stops being a limitation and becomes your *focus model*. Opening the nav over the dashboard = make nav the active screen; the dashboard's canvas keeps showing its last frame behind it (frozen, briefly — fine for a drawer). Close nav → reactivate dashboard, it resumes live. Touch "just works" because the focused thing is always the active Legato screen.

## Recommended structure
- **Top-level `ui_manager` (the thing that ties it together).** Owns the canvas/LCDC **layer pool**, the surface↔layer mapping, the **active-view + overlay stack**, and view transitions. This is what the compositor's *mechanism* becomes — promoted from "the UI module" to "the resource/orchestration layer."
- **Per-view modules** (`ui/dashboard`, `ui/songlist`, `ui/gameplay_select` …). Each owns its view's content, event wiring, and state. Its **composition root is that screen's On-Show hook** (where it runtime-registers its widget callbacks — exactly the DI pattern from before). One MGS Screen per view → clean authoring.
- **Overlay modules** (`ui/nav`). An overlay is a view that the `ui_manager` shows *on top of* the current one (own OVR layer); when open it takes focus (becomes the active Legato screen), background parks.

So: `ui_manager` knows about layers and "show view X / push overlay Y"; each view/overlay module knows only its own widgets. The current `compositor.c` splits into `ui_manager` (canvas/layer plumbing) + `ui/dashboard` + `ui/nav`.

## The one fork I'd want your call on
The "background parks/freezes while an overlay or dialog is up" model is clean and cheap — **but it assumes nothing behind an overlay needs to keep updating live.** Is that true for marvin? For the nav drawer, certainly. For a dialog over the dashboard — if you'd want live telemetry still ticking behind a modal, that breaks the model and we'd instead keep one persistent "shell" screen with overlays as *layers within it* (dashboard always live, no screen-switch). 

My lean: **freeze-the-background is fine** for marvin (overlays are brief, the camera — the one always-live thing — is already independent on HEO), so go with per-view Legato Screens + the focus model. But if you foresee "live dashboard visible behind a non-modal panel," tell me and we keep a persistent shell instead.

If this framing sounds right, I'll write it up properly — promote `ui_compositor.md` into a `ui_architecture.md` (or expand it) with the `ui_manager` + per-view module model and the focus/parking rule, plus a journal decision — and we can stage the `compositor.c` → `ui_manager` split as the first refactor. Want me to, or do you want to push on the fork first?

Good news: what you want — telemetry staying live while the nav is open — **isn't actually the freeze model. It's what you already have.** Let me untangle that, because it changes the recommendation slightly.

## Your live-telemetry case is "overlay-as-layer," not "switch screen"
Right now the dashboard is the active Legato screen (rendering every frame) and the nav is an **OVR layer within that same screen**. So while the nav drawer is open on the left, the dashboard stays the active screen and the **uncovered right-side telemetry keeps updating**. You're already getting live-under-nav — no freeze. Freeze would only happen if we made the nav a *separate* focus-screen, which we specifically should **not** do for the dashboard, precisely because of your telemetry need.

So the model isn't global "freeze vs live." It's **per-interaction**, and there are two distinct verbs:
- **Overlay-as-layer** (nav over dashboard): background stays the live active screen; overlay is another layer in it. → live telemetry. ✅
- **Switch-view** (dashboard ↔ songlist dialog): a full-screen view *replaces* another; the outgoing one parks/freezes — fine, because you're not watching telemetry while picking a song.

Use the first for the nav, the second for dialogs. You don't pick one mode.

## Can we shift later? Yes, without extreme difficulty — if we keep one boundary clean
The insurance is the **`ui_manager` API**: per-view modules call `ui_manager_show_view(X)` / `ui_manager_push_overlay(Y)` and **never** call `legato_showScreen` or the canvas APIs directly. Then whether a given interaction is implemented as overlay-layer or switch-view is an internal manager detail — flipping one later is a manager change, not a per-module rewrite.

Honest cost breakdown of any future shift:
- **C side: cheap** — contained in `ui_manager`, if the boundary holds.
- **MGS side: the real cost** — moving widgets between Screens, or duplicating a cross-screen overlay, is manual re-authoring in the designer. That's the part that takes redo work, not the firmware.

So: don't over-commit the MGS Screen structure early, route everything through `ui_manager`, and you stay flexible. The hard ceiling on "how many things live at once" stays the LCDC layers (3 UI + camera) — budget dashboard BASE + nav OVR1 + one spare OVR2.

## Net plan
- **Keep nav as a live layer over the dashboard** (preserves your telemetry) — formalize, don't change.
- **Songlist/gameplay-select = switch-view** to their own MGS Screens (freeze the dashboard behind, which is fine).
- **`ui_manager`** owns both verbs + the layer budget; per-view modules own only their widgets, wired from their On-Show composition root.
- Cross-screen nav: revisit when we add the second full-screen view — likely the nav is reachable from the dashboard shell, and dialogs get a back affordance rather than the full drawer. We don't need to solve it now.

If that lands, I'll write it up as `ui_architecture.md` (the two verbs + the focus/park-vs-live-layer rule + the `ui_manager`/per-view split) and a journal decision, then we can stage the `compositor.c` → `ui_manager` + `ui/dashboard` + `ui/nav` split as the first refactor. Want me to write the doc, or keep discussing?

leResult leAddRootWidget(leWidget* wgt,
                         uint32_t layerIdx)
{
    leLayerState* layer;

    if(wgt == NULL || layerIdx >= _state.layerList.size)
        return LE_FAILURE;

    layer = (leLayerState*)leList_Get(&_state.layerList, layerIdx);

    leRenderer_DamageArea(&wgt->rect, layerIdx);

    return LE_OCALL(layer->root, addChild, wgt);
}

That settles it — `leRemoveRootWidget` exists alongside `leAddRootWidget`, so **a widget tree can be re-hosted onto any layer at runtime.** Combined with the global-layerList fact, this gives you everything you asked for. Here's the concrete answer.

## The model that satisfies all your constraints

Three Legato layers, each its own canvas, all rendering live every frame:

| Legato layer | LCDC | Content | Lifecycle |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | BASE | active full-screen view (dashboard, …) | swappable via `legato_showScreen` (replaces) |
| 1 | OVR1 | **nav** | resident — attached once, never torn down |
| 2 | OVR2 | **song-select modal** (sized to the dialog rect) | shown/hidden, but background stays live |
| — | HEO | camera | video.c, outside Legato |

- **Nav on its own resident layer ⇒ "same nav on every view" for free.** It's independent of layer 0, so switching the base view (`legato_showScreen` only touches the outgoing view's layer-0 root) leaves the nav untouched. Author it once.
- **Modal dialog on OVR2, sized to the dialog, dashboard live on BASE behind it ⇒ uncovered telemetry keeps updating.** Exactly your requirement — and it's only invoked from the dashboard, which fits.
- **No freeze for overlays** because we never `legato_showScreen` them. Freeze is reserved for true full-screen base-view *replacement*, where it's fine.

## Your MGS-baggage concern, addressed directly

An MGS Screen brings two things:
1. **Switch machinery** — `screenID` enum, `legato_showScreen`, the show/hide switch table. For overlays you **just don't call it.** It's inert generated code, not harmful — it sits unused.
2. **`screenInit`/`screenShow` attach the tree's root to the layer index it was authored on** (MGS counts layers from 0, so every standalone Screen wants layer 0 → they'd collide).

That collision is the *only* real friction, and `leRemoveRootWidget` + `leAddRootWidget` dissolve it: build the tree via the screen's init/show, then **re-host its root onto the target layer**. So an MGS Screen becomes, in effect, a clean "widget-tree factory" you place wherever you want. You get the separate-design-canvas workflow you prefer, and the switch baggage stays dormant.

## Who owns what
- **`ui_manager`** — owns the layer/canvas pool, calls each panel's init, **re-hosts roots onto the right layer**, and exposes the verbs: `show_view(X)` (replace layer 0), `push_overlay(nav|dialog)` (show its resident/own layer), `hide_overlay(...)`. This is where the "which layer, switch-vs-coexist" decisions live — so your reversibility worry is covered: changing a panel from coexist to replace is a `ui_manager` change, not a rewrite.
- **Per-panel modules** (`ui/dashboard`, `ui/nav`, `ui/song_select`) — own only their widgets + interactions, wired from their own On-Show composition root.

## One config change
`LE_LAYER_COUNT` 2 → 3 (map Legato 0/1/2 → BASE/OVR1/OVR2; HEO stays video's, not a Legato layer). `XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS` is already 4. Note the ceiling this puts you at: dashboard + nav + dialog + camera = **all 4 LCDC layers**. A 4th *simultaneous* UI surface would need canvas multiplexing (`baseCanvasID` swap) — fine, just know the wall is there.

---

This is solvable now and maps cleanly onto what's confirmed in the code. I'd like to write it up as `ui_architecture.md` (the layer model, the "MGS Screen as re-hosted widget-tree factory" technique, the `ui_manager` verbs + per-panel split, the layer budget) plus a journal decision, then sequence the refactor:

1. `LE_LAYER_COUNT` 2→3 + map OVR2.
2. Split `compositor.c` → `ui_manager` + `ui/dashboard` + `ui/nav` (re-host nav onto layer 1).
3. Author song-select as its own MGS Screen; `ui_manager` hosts it on layer 2 as a modal.

Confirmed — both pieces survive and we now own the startup:

- **String table is still there**: `extern const leStringTable stringTable` + `void initializeStrings(void)` in `le_gen_assets.h`. We must now call `leSetStringTable(&stringTable)` + `initializeStrings()` ourselves (the deleted init did this — without it, no text renders).
- **`screenUpdate_Marvin` is effectively a no-op** (`setSize(root, current_w, current_h)` ×2 — sets size to itself; `LE_DRIVER_LAYER_MODE` + `leUpdate` already handle layer rects). We can skip calling it per-frame.
- **Nobody shows the screen now** (the `manual_input.c` hit is just a comment). So as regenerated, **the screen is blank** — `Legato_Initialize` no longer shows anything.

## So this is a net win — with one required wiring step now

What `ui_manager` (or, minimally, `Compositor_Initialize` for now) must call once at startup, after `Legato_Initialize`, before the first `leUpdate` (i.e. from `APP_Initialize`, pre-scheduler):

```c
leSetStringTable(&stringTable);   // from le_gen_assets.h
initializeStrings();
screenInit_Marvin();              // builds the widget trees
screenShow_Marvin();              // attaches roots to layers + fires Marvin_OnShow
```

`screenShow_Marvin` is what attaches `root0`→layer 0 and `root1`→layer 1 and raises `Marvin_OnShow` (which already runs our nav/canvas setup). So the composition-root pattern is intact — we just trigger it explicitly now.

This is exactly the orchestration `ui_manager` will own, and the framework now blesses it (the `// call to show this screen` comment flip). For the multi-screen model: `ui_manager` calls `screenInit_*` for dashboard/nav/dialog, `screenShow_*` to attach, re-hosts nav→layer 1 and dialog→layer 2 with `leRemoveRootWidget`/`leAddRootWidget`, and leaves them resident → all live, no switching. Exactly what we designed, now with no baggage at all.

## Next step — your call on scope
Because the screen is blank until we add those four calls, we need to wire it regardless. Two ways to take it:

- **(a) Minimal un-blank now** — add the four calls to `Compositor_Initialize` so the dashboard + nav come back, build/verify the state-machine-off path works, then commit. Small, low-risk.
- **(b) Do it as the `ui_manager` refactor** — introduce `ui_manager` owning string-table + screen orchestration (init/show/re-host/visibility), split `compositor.c` accordingly, and write the `ui_architecture.md` + journal decision first so the design is locked.

I'd suggest **(a) right now** to get back to a working, verifiable state and commit it (the regen shouldn't sit half-wired), then **(b)** as a focused refactor on top. Want me to do (a) — add the startup calls to `Compositor_Initialize` — now?

## What this change does (one logical unit)
- **MGS regen** (state machine off): deletes `le_gen_init.{c,h}`, strips the `legato_*ScreenState` calls from `le_gen_harmony.c`, flips the screen functions to "call directly."
- **Compat stub** `default/src/compat/gfx/legato/generated/le_gen_init.h` — provides the 5 includes the old header exposed; lives **outside** the regenerated tree, added to the include path in `user.cmake`. The regenerated `le_gen_harmony.h` keeps its `#include le_gen_init.h` (restored to MGS form — no manual patch) and resolves to the stub. Future regens need **zero hand-patching**.
- **`compositor.c`** owns screen startup (`leSetStringTable` + `initializeStrings` + `screenInit_Marvin` + `screenShow_Marvin`).

`le_gen_harmony.h` is back to its committed form (restored from git), so it's not even in the diff — the stub does all the work. The resolution is safe: the compat copy is only found when the generated one is absent (state machine off); if it's ever re-enabled, the generated copy in its own directory wins.

## Why this is a good outcome
You've now got **zero screen-state baggage** *and* it's regen-proof. This is the clean foundation for the `ui_manager` refactor — we own screen orchestration outright (init/show/re-host onto layers), with no MGS machinery to work around.

Not committed — build + eyeball the dashboard/nav first (this regen must be committed *with* the wiring + stub as one unit; the regen alone is a blank screen). When it's verified, I'll stage the whole set (deleted `le_gen_init.*`, the compat stub, `user.cmake`, `compositor.c`, the regenerated `le_gen_*`) and commit.

Two follow-ups for later (not now): this MGS-bug workaround deserves a journal note alongside the `drv_image_sensor.h` shim precedent, and it folds naturally into the `ui_architecture.md` write-up + the `ui_manager` refactor we lined up.

```text
1	# marvin — UI compositor (canvas surface pool)
2	
3	Design for marvin's operator-UI presentation layer: **pre-render UI panels into RAM
4	surfaces, then multiplex the scarce LCDC hardware layers across them** so a panel can
5	be brought up (or slid in) instantly without re-rendering or disturbing what is behind
6	it. Built on Microchip's **GFX Canvas** component as the surface/layer substrate, with
7	Legato kept as the rendering engine (fonts, draw primitives, the `song_list` widget).
8	
9	Read [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.5 (operator UI) and §4.1 (video/display) first; this doc is
10	the authoritative design for the compositor specifically. Status: **design — not yet
11	built.** Decision recorded in [`journal.md`](journal.md) (2026-06-25).
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. The core idea
16	
17	Today, content geometry is welded to hardware layers 1:1:1 — a Legato layer renders into
18	exactly one framebuffer, which is exactly one LCDC layer. There are only **4 LCDC layers**
19	on the SAM9X75 XLCDC (`BASE`, `OVR1`, `HEO`, `OVR2`), and one (`HEO`) is owned by the live
20	camera. That is too few to give every UI panel a permanent layer.
21	
22	The compositor breaks the welding:
23	
24	- A **surface** is a chunk of RAM (a framebuffer) holding pre-rendered pixels. Surfaces are
25	  cheap — we can keep many resident.
26	- A **layer** is a scarce hardware compositor window. We have **two free** ones (`OVR1`,
27	  `OVR2`) plus `BASE`.
28	- Bringing a panel up = point a free layer at a surface and enable it (register writes, no
29	  render). Hiding = disable the layer. Sliding = animate the layer's window position. The
30	  surface's pixels persist, so none of this re-renders anything or touches the layers below.
31	
32	This is exactly what the **GFX Canvas** component provides, and it is the one capability the
33	plain layer registers cannot give us: canvas redirects Legato's render target to an arbitrary
34	off-screen buffer (a "canvas object"), independent of which hardware layer — if any — that
35	buffer is currently shown on.
36	
37	## 2. Why canvas (and why not the alternatives)
38	
39	How Legato renders today (confirmed in `legato_renderer.c` + `drv_gfx_xlcdc.c`): Legato
40	paints damaged tiles into a **scratch buffer**, then `DRV_XLCDC_BlitBuffer` copies each tile
41	into `drvLayer[activeLayer].pixelBuffer` — the framebuffer of whatever layer is currently
42	*active* (`GFX_IOCTL_SET_ACTIVE_LAYER`). **The only knob deciding where Legato's pixels land
43	is the active layer's `pixelBuffer.pixels` pointer.** There is no stock Legato API for
44	"render this widget tree into that arbitrary buffer."
45	
46	- **GFX Canvas (chosen).** `GFXC_GetPixelBuffer()` hands Legato the *canvas object's* buffer
47	  instead of a fixed layer framebuffer, and `gfxcSetBaseCanvasID` switches which canvas a
48	  Legato layer renders into. That is precisely "many pre-rendered surfaces in RAM,
49	  multiplexed onto few layers." It also brings layer binding (`gfxcSetLayer`), show/hide,
50	  window position/size/alpha, and hardware-stepped fade/move effects — all generated.
51	- **DIY pixel-buffer retarget (rejected).** We could mutate the active layer's
52	  `pixelBuffer.pixels` ourselves before each render and park the buffer afterward. Viable
53	  (~100–200 LOC) but it reimplements the bookkeeping canvas already does (per-surface size,
54	  scratch tiling, layer binding) — and once surfaces are non-full-screen it grows. Not worth
55	  maintaining a hand-rolled half of canvas.
56	- **Direct layer control only (insufficient).** The XLCDC PLIB exposes everything needed to
57	  *present and animate* a layer (`XLCDC_SetLayerAddress/WindowXYPos/WindowXYSize/Opts/Enable`,
58	  each with a deferred-commit flag). This is the right tool for the **slide/show/hide**, and
59	  the compositor uses it (or canvas's wrappers over it). What it cannot do is get Legato
60	  widget content *into* an off-screen surface in the first place — that is the canvas half.
61	
62	So the split is: **canvas owns "render content into a surface and bind a surface to a
63	layer"; direct layer control (via canvas's effect engine or our own stepper) owns "move it."**
64	
65	## 3. Hardware layer budget
66	
67	| LCDC layer | Owner | Notes |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| `BASE`  | Compositor — persistent background / main dashboard | Always on; bottom of the stack. |
70	| `OVR1`  | Compositor — swappable overlay A | **To be enabled** (`XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS` is 2 today = BASE+HEO). |
71	| `OVR2`  | Compositor — swappable overlay B | **To be enabled.** |
72	| `HEO`   | **Video capture** (`video.c`) — live camera | Re-pointed every frame in the ISC ISR; the scaler lives here. **Off-limits to the compositor.** |
73	
74	So at any instant the stack is: `BASE` (background) + up to two overlay panels (`OVR1`/`OVR2`)
75	+ the camera (`HEO`), composited in hardware. We can keep *many* surfaces pre-rendered in RAM
76	and choose which two overlays are bound/visible at a time.
77	
78	> Latent config item: the stock generated `Marvin` screen maps Legato layer 1 → `HEO`
79	> (a 320×800 root). That conflicts with video owning `HEO`. Under this design the two Legato
80	> layers must map to `BASE` + an `OVR`, never `HEO`. Reconcile during bring-up (§8).
81	
82	## 4. Architecture
83	
84	```
85	                 ┌──────────── marvin compositor (new module, ui/) ───────────┐
86	                 │  surface registry  │  panel state machine  │  touch router  │
87	                 └───────┬───────────────────────┬───────────────────┬────────┘
88	                         │ render into surface    │ bind/show/slide   │ route touch
89	                 ┌───────▼────────┐      ┌────────▼─────────┐   ┌─────▼───────┐
90	   Legato  ──────►  GFX Canvas    │      │   GFX Canvas      │   │ Legato pick │
91	 (fonts,         │  gfxcGetPixel  │      │ gfxcSetLayer/Show │   │  (live only)│
92	  song_list,     │  Buffer → surf │      │ /Position/Move    │   └─────────────┘
93	  string render) └───────┬────────┘      └────────┬──────────┘
94	                         │ canvas objects (static, non-cached RAM surfaces)
95	                 ┌───────▼───────────────────────▼──────────┐
96	                 │      XLCDC driver — per-layer IOCTLs      │   HEO: driven directly
97	                 │   BASE / OVR1 / OVR2  (canvas-managed)    │   by video.c (camera)
98	                 └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
99	```
100	
101	### 4.1 Surfaces
102	A fixed pool of **canvas objects**, each given a **statically allocated, non-cached** buffer
103	(`gfxcSetPixelBuffer(id, w, h, mode, &static_buf)`) sized to its panel — not necessarily
104	full-screen. RGB565 to match the panel and halve memory; ARGB8888 only for a surface that
105	needs per-pixel alpha over the camera (most fades use the layer's *global* alpha instead).
106	
107	### 4.2 The compositor module (marvin-owned, in `ui/`)
108	A thin module over the canvas API, following the MCC-isolation idiom (own files added via
109	`user.cmake`, no edits to the generated tree). It owns:
110	- the **surface registry** — logical panel (song list, nav menu, dashboard, dialog) → canvas id;
111	- a small **panel state machine** — `render → park → present(layer) → (interact) → hide`;
112	- the **touch router** (§5).
113	
114	### 4.3 Rendering content into a surface
115	To (re)render a panel's widget tree into its surface, point Legato at that canvas group
116	(`gfxcSetBaseCanvasID`) and drive one Legato render. The `song_list` widget and Legato's
117	string/scheme renderers are reused verbatim. Rendering happens **only when the panel's
118	content is dirty** (new model, scroll, selection) — not per display frame. The rendered
119	pixels then sit parked in the surface indefinitely.
120	
121	### 4.4 Presenting / animating
122	- **Instant reveal:** `gfxcSetLayer(id, OVRx)` + `gfxcShowCanvas(id)` (+ position/size). No render.
123	- **Hide:** `gfxcHideCanvas(id)`.
124	- **Slide:** `gfxcStartEffectMove(...)` (canvas's stepped tween) or our own vsync stepper over
125	  `gfxcSetWindowPosition`. Off-edge slides need window clipping (`CONFIG_CANVAS_ENABLE_WINDOW_CLIPPING`,
126	  on by default) so the layer window stays within display bounds.
127	- **Fade:** layer global alpha ramp (`gfxcStartEffectFade`).
128	
129	## 5. Touch routing — the key constraint
130	
131	Legato delivers touch by hit-testing the **active screen's widget tree** (`legato_input.c`
132	→ layer roots). A *parked* surface bound to `OVR1` shows pixels but is **not** in Legato's
133	screen tree, so Legato will not route touches to it. This is the one thing the surface-pool
134	model does not get for free, and it must be designed, not discovered.
135	
136	**Rule:** a surface is interactive **only while it is the live render target of a Legato
137	layer** positioned where it is shown. Parked snapshots are for fast presentation and
138	transitions (reveal, slide, background), not interaction.
139	
140	**Recommended model — reveal-then-promote:** bring a panel up instantly from its parked
141	surface; when it must become interactive, **promote** it — make its canvas the active Legato
142	layer's render target (`gfxcSetBaseCanvasID`), align the layer to its on-screen position, and
143	render live. Promotion is cheap (register writes + one render). `song_list` already
144	hit-tests internally, so the live path needs only Legato's event *delivery*, which promotion
145	restores. (Alternative, deferred: a marvin-owned input dispatcher reading maxtouch and
146	mapping coords → topmost visible surface → element, bypassing Legato's screen model
147	entirely. More control, more code; revisit only if promotion proves awkward.)
148	
149	## 6. Memory budget
150	
151	`.region_nocache` is **32 MB** and is *shared* with the ISC capture pool — account for both:
152	
153	| Consumer | Size (approx) |
154	|---|---|
155	| ISC capture pool (4 × 1280×720 × 3 B, BGR888) | ~10.5 MB |
156	| Legato scratch (`LE_SCRATCH_BUFFER_SIZE_KB` 512) | 0.5 MB |
157	| `BASE` surface (1280×800 × 2 B, RGB565) | ~2.0 MB |
158	| Overlay surfaces (RGB565, sized to panel) | song list ~700×800 ≈ 1.1 MB; nav menu ~320×800 ≈ 0.5 MB; dialog/metadata each ≈ 0.5–2 MB |
159	
160	Full-screen RGB565 = **~2.0 MB**; most overlays are well under that. With ~21 MB free after
161	the capture pool and scratch, memory is **not** the binding constraint — the **two free
162	overlay layers** are. Size surfaces to their content, prefer RGB565, and set
163	`CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ` to the number of distinct surfaces we pre-cache (≥ the panel count,
164	not the layer count).
165	
166	## 7. Static-allocation & cache rules
167	
168	- **Static buffers.** Canvas's default config allocates nothing (NULL buffers). Every canvas
169	  surface gets a file-scope static array in `.region_nocache`, passed via `gfxcSetPixelBuffer`.
170	  No malloc — consistent with the project rule. ([static-allocation rule](journal.md))
171	- **Non-cached.** Surfaces are CPU-rendered then read by the LCDC DMA / 2D engine, so they
172	  must be non-cached, same as the framebuffer (`FB_CACHE_NC`) and the Legato scratch (the
173	  2026-06-24 cache-coherency fix). Note CPU writes to non-cached DDR are slow; rendering is
174	  occasional (dirty-only), so this is acceptable — re-measure if a full-surface repaint
175	  shows up hot.
176	- **FX task.** The generated `GFX_CANVAS_Task` uses dynamic `xTaskCreate` (like the other MCC
177	  XLCDC/USB tasks on heap_1). Either convert to `xTaskCreateStatic` or accept it alongside
178	  the existing MCC dynamic tasks; log the choice as an MCC re-apply patch. The task is
179	  **required even with FX off** — it drives the `GFXC_INIT → RUNNING` transition, and
180	  `gfxcShowCanvas`/update return early until `RUNNING`.
181	- **Task priority = 2 (UI band).** Set the gfx_canvas component's *Task Priority* field to **2**
182	  so the task joins marvin's UI tier (`LEGATO`/`XLCDC`/`DRV_MAXTOUCH`/`SYS_INPUT`; see the
183	  2026-05-21 priority re-tiering in [`journal.md`](journal.md)). The generated default of 1 is
184	  wrong — band 1 is reserved for future housekeeping, and the canvas task is an active
185	  UI-critical-path stage (it commits Legato's output to the layers). Set it in the component
186	  yml, not `tasks.c`, so regen reproduces it with no re-apply patch. Stack 1024 / 10 ms delay
187	  are fine (match the other UI tasks); FX is off so it mostly idles between updates.
188	
189	## 8. MCC configuration & re-apply notes
190	
191	The canvas component re-architects the display path (canvas becomes Legato's
192	`gfxDriverInterface`; XLCDC's own struct → `xlcdcDisplayDriver`; the static `frame_buffer`
193	array is removed; a per-layer IOCTL subset is added; `GFX_CANVAS_Initialize` + the FX task
194	are wired in). Steps:
195	
196	1. **Enable `OVR1` + `OVR2`** in the XLCDC driver (`XLCDC_TOT_LAYERS` 2→4, `layerOrder`) so
197	   the compositor has its two overlay layers. Keep `HEO` for video.
198	2. **Add the GFX Canvas component**, set `CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ` to our surface count, default
199	   color mode RGB565, and give each object a static non-cached buffer (replace the generated
200	   `gfxcSetPixelBuffer(..., NULL)` template with our buffers + real sizes).
201	3. **Reconcile the Legato layer→hardware-layer mapping** so the two Legato layers map to
202	   `BASE` + an `OVR`, never `HEO` (§3 latent item).
203	4. **Verify `video.c`/HEO is undisturbed** by the canvas/XLCDC init reorder (canvas inits all
204	   layers disabled; video sets up HEO at runtime — confirm ordering doesn't clobber it).
205	5. Add the canvas/FX-task choices to the MCC re-apply patch list (cache/scratch `-D`, task
206	   static conversion, layer-count, buffer wiring).
207	
208	## 9. Phased plan
209	
210	- **P0 — substrate.** Enable OVR1/OVR2; add the canvas component with static non-cached
211	  surfaces; get a blank `BASE` + one OVR rendering through canvas (display still works).
212	- **P1 — compositor module.** `ui/compositor.{h,c}`: surface registry + present/hide/bind over
213	  the canvas API; a console command to bind/show/hide a test surface on OVR1. Reuse `song_list`.
214	- **P2 — pre-render + instant reveal.** Render the song list into its surface once; bind to
215	  OVR1 and reveal/hide instantly; confirm no re-render and BASE untouched.
216	- **P3 — slide + nav menu.** Nav-menu surface on OVR2; slide in/out (canvas move effect or our
217	  stepper); off-edge clipping verified.
218	- **P4 — touch promotion.** Reveal-then-promote so the song list is interactive once shown;
219	  scroll/select validated on hardware.
220	- **P5 — panel set.** Generalize to the §4.5 surfaces (dashboard, metadata, dialog); finalize
221	  the surface count + memory budget.
222	
223	## 10. Open questions
224	
225	- **Touch model:** is reveal-then-promote (§5) sufficient, or do we need a marvin-owned
226	  maxtouch dispatcher? Decide at P4.
227	- **`GFX_CANVAS_Task` static conversion** vs. accepting it as an MCC dynamic task.
228	- **Surface count / sizes** (`CONFIG_CANVAS_NUM_OBJ`, per-panel dimensions) — lock at P5
229	  against the real panel set and the shared `.region_nocache` budget.
230	- **HEO ↔ canvas coexistence:** confirm canvas's layer init/IOCTL path never touches HEO and
231	  the init reorder doesn't disturb video's runtime HEO setup.
232	- **Per-pixel alpha:** which surfaces (if any) need ARGB8888 over the camera vs. layer global
233	  alpha.
234	
235	## 11. Relationship to spec §4.5 / Q5
236	
237	This is the concrete answer to spec **Q5** (Legato vs. custom UI) for the *presentation*
238	layer: **keep Legato as the renderer, add a thin marvin compositor over GFX Canvas for
239	surface/layer management.** It does not change how individual screens are *authored* (MGS /
240	custom widgets) — only how their rendered output is cached in RAM and composited onto the
241	panel's hardware layers.
242
